transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I guess I just haven’t been quite myself lately. It’s not anything too dramatic, I don’t want to make a big fuss, but I don’t seem to have the push I used to. I used to do choir, and quilting, and go visit folks, and now most days I just sit at home with the TV on low… even when I know people are expecting me. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
How long have you been feeling this way—weeks, months, or longer?

I suppose it’s been longer than weeks… probably since I retired from the school office, a little over two years ago. It sort of built up slowly, so I didn’t think much of it at first. Is that helpful?
Over this same time, have you or others noticed any changes in your memory, such as forgetting recent conversations, misplacing things more often, or having trouble concentrating?

I don’t think so… not in any big way. I mean, I might walk into a room and forget why, but I think everybody does that some, don’t they? I haven’t noticed forgetting conversations or anything serious. My concentration maybe isn’t what it used to be, but I figured that was just me getting older. Is that the sort of thing you’re asking?
Over these past two years, have you noticed changes in your sleep or appetite, or times when you felt unusually tired, worthless, or guilty for no clear reason?

I’m not really sure… I don’t think there’s been anything too out of the ordinary. Sleep comes and goes a bit, but nothing I’d want to make sound worse than it is. Appetite’s about the same, I think. I do get tired, but I figured that’s just age and not doing as much. I wouldn’t say I feel worthless or guilty for no reason… not really. Is that okay?
Over these past two years, has your mood stayed pretty much the same the whole time, or have there been certain weeks or months when it felt noticeably worse than at other times?

I’m not sure I could point to certain weeks or months, no. It’s been more… about the same, I think. Maybe some days feel heavier than others, but I haven’t noticed a real spell where my mood was much worse for a long time. Does that answer it alright?
Over these past two years, have you often felt hopeless about things, or noticed your self-esteem being lower than it used to be?

I don’t think I’ve felt hopeless, not really. I mean, I have my moments where I get discouraged, but I wouldn’t want to say it’s been often. My self-esteem… I suppose it’s not something I think about much. I don’t feel especially down on myself, I don’t think. Is that the kind of answer you mean?
Over these past two years, would you say that on most days, your low mood or lack of motivation has been there for the greater part of the day, rather than just coming and going?

I guess… yes, in a way. I don’t know if I’d call it “low mood” exactly, but most days I just don’t seem to have the push I used to. I used to go to choir, do my quilting, visit folks, and now a lot of days I just sit at home with the TV on low, even when I know people are kind of expecting me. It’s not all day every day, but it’s there a lot. Is that what you mean?
During these past two years, has there ever been a stretch of two months or more when you felt pretty much back to your normal self, with your motivation and mood returning to how they used to be?

I don’t think there’s been a full two months where I felt just like my old self, no. It’s sort of been building since I retired from the school office, a little over two years ago. Not terrible all at once, just… I haven’t really gotten back to how I was before. Does that make sense?
